title: Phase 2 · Stage 6: Members and loans
summary: Model genres and membership tiers as enums, members and loans as records, and lend books to real people with due dates.

steps.title: Enums and records
body: Shelfwise is about to meet **people**. Two new kinds of type fit what you need.
An **enum** is a fixed set of named choices. A member is *Standard* or *Premium*, nothing else, and the compiler now knows it:
```csharp fragment
enum MemberTier { Standard, Premium }
enum Genre { General, Fiction, Mystery, Science, History, Children }
foreach (var g in Enum.GetValues<Genre>()) ...     // every choice, in order
string.Join(", ", Enum.GetNames<Genre>())          // "General, Fiction, ..."
A **record** is a type for **data**: one line declares the properties, a constructor, value equality and a readable `ToString`:
```csharp fragment
record Member(int Id, string Name, string Email, MemberTier Tier);
var ada = new Member(1, "Ada Lovelace", "ada@example.com", MemberTier.Premium);
Console.WriteLine(ada.Name);              // Ada Lovelace

Why a record for members but a class for books? A `Book` **changes** (copies go out and come back) and guards that with methods. A member's details are just facts. Records are immutable by default: to "change" one you make a copy with `with`:
```csharp fragment
var upgraded = ada with { Tier = MemberTier.Standard };   // ada itself is untouched
You can still override `ToString` in a record to choose how it prints.

steps.prompt: Records compare by value. What does this print?
code: var c = a with { Tier = MemberTier.Standard };
record Member(int Id, string Name, MemberTier Tier);
steps.explain: Two records with the same values are equal, even though they are different objects. `with` copies `a` and changes one property.

steps.title: Genres and members
prompt: Add two enums and a record at the bottom of the file:
enum Genre { General, Fiction, Mystery, Science, History, Children }
record Member(int Id, string Name, string Email, MemberTier Tier);

**Genres.** `add` takes an optional sixth field: `add isbn|title|author|year|copies|genre` (any case). Without it the genre is `General`. A bad genre prints `Error: genre must be one of General, Fiction, Mystery, Science, History, Children` (build that list with `Enum.GetNames`). The usage error becomes `Error: use add isbn|title|author|year|copies[|genre]`. `Book` gets a `Genre` property (constructor parameter `Genre genre = Genre.General`) and its line shows it before the copies:
978-0261103344 | The Hobbit | J.R.R. Tolkien | 1937 | Fiction | 3/3 in
**Members.** Keep a `List<Member>`. Ids start at 1 and go up.
- `join name|email` or `join name|email|tier` (tier in any case, default `Standard`) prints `Member 1: Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com> (Premium)` (override `ToString` in the record).

- Errors, first one only: wrong number of fields `Error: use join name|email[|tier]`; blank name `Error: name is required`; an email without `@` `Error: "adaexample.com" is not a valid email address`; bad tier `Error: tier must be Standard or Premium`.
- `members` prints every member in id order, or `No members yet.`
`help` becomes `Commands: add, list, find, authors, join, members, lend, return, stats, fine, help, quit`.

hints: Add `out Genre genre` to `ValidateBook`, give it a default (`genre = Genre.General;`) and only parse when `parts.Length == 6`.

A `TryParseGenre(string text, out Genre genre)` that loops over `Enum.GetValues<Genre>()` and compares `candidate.ToString()` with `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase` avoids accepting numbers. Write `TryParseTier` the same way.

steps.title: A loan is a record of an event
body: Lending used to mean *one fewer copy on the shelf*. A real library needs to know **who** has it and **until when**. That is a `Loan`: a small record of something that happened.
```csharp
record Loan(int Id, string Isbn, int MemberId, DateOnly LoanedOn, DateOnly DueOn, DateOnly? ReturnedOn = null)
public bool IsActive => ReturnedOn is null;
- `DateOnly` is a calendar date with no time of day, perfect for due dates. `today.AddDays(14)` is two weeks later.
- `DateOnly?` means *a date, or nothing yet*: a loan that has not come back has no return date.
- Returning does not delete the loan (the history matters for reports later). It **replaces** it with a copy that has a return date: `loans[i] = loan with { ReturnedOn = today };`

Shelfwise never asks the computer for the date: output must be the same on every run. Today is a variable that starts at **Monday 2 March 2026**, and later stages will move it forward. Always print dates as `{date:yyyy-MM-dd}`, because the default format depends on the culture.

code: var loan = new Loan(1, today, today.AddDays(14));
var back = loan with { ReturnedOn = today.AddDays(3) };
record Loan(int Id, DateOnly LoanedOn, DateOnly DueOn, DateOnly? ReturnedOn = null)
public bool IsActive => ReturnedOn is null;
steps.explain: 14 days after 2 March is 16 March. `with` made a new loan with a return date; the original is still active.

steps.title: Lend to members
prompt: Lending now needs a member, and records a `Loan`.
1. Add `DateOnly today = new DateOnly(2026, 3, 2);` near the top, a `List<Loan>`, and the `Loan` record from the card at the bottom.

2. `lend <isbn> <memberId>`: if there are not exactly two words, `Error: use lend <isbn> <memberId>`. An id that is not a number or not a member: `Error: no member with id 7`. Then the book checks as before. On success add a loan (ids start at 1) due **14 days** from today and print `Lent: The Hobbit to Ada Lovelace, due 2026-03-16 (2/3 in)`.

3. `return <isbn> <memberId>`: same usage and lookups (`Error: use return <isbn> <memberId>`). Find that member's **active** loan of that book, or print `Error: Ada Lovelace does not have The Hobbit`. Otherwise put the copy back, set the loan's return date to today with `with`, and print `Returned: The Hobbit from Ada Lovelace (3/3 in)`.
4. `loans` prints every active loan: `#1 The Hobbit -> Ada Lovelace, due 2026-03-16`, or `No active loans.`
`help` becomes `Commands: add, list, find, authors, join, members, lend, return, loans, stats, fine, help, quit`. Look members up by id with a small `Member? FindMember(string text)` method.

require.message: Uses with to record the return

hints: Both commands start the same way: `string[] words = text.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);`, check `words.Length != 2`, look up the member, then the book.
Lending: `var loan = new Loan(loans.Count + 1, book.Isbn, member.Id, today, today.AddDays(14)); loans.Add(loan);`. Print the due date with `{loan.DueOn:yyyy-MM-dd}`.
Returning: loop with an index so you can replace the loan: `loans[i] = loan with { ReturnedOn = today };` after `book.TryReturn();`.
